name: Personal Finance Practice
description: A small example set that applies percentage skills to discounts, tips, and tax.
author: QuickMaths

track.name: Personal Finance Practice
track.description: Use percentages in everyday money decisions.

skills.name: Discounts, tips, and tax
skills.description: Calculate percentage increases and decreases in practical money situations.
skills.theory:
A percentage describes a part out of 100. Convert a percentage to a decimal before multiplying.

Discount: sale price = original price × (1 - discount rate).

Tip or tax: total = starting amount × (1 + rate).

Estimate first so you can catch calculator or decimal-place mistakes.

examples.prompt: A €40 item is 25% off. What is the sale price?
examples.explanation: 25% of 40 is 10, so subtract 10 from 40. Equivalently, 40 × 0.75 = 30.

applications.title: Shopping
applications.description: Compare sale prices and decide whether a discount is actually useful.

applications.title: Budgeting
applications.description: Estimate tax, tips, fees, and price increases before spending.

problems.prompt: A €50 jacket is 20% off. Enter the sale price without the currency symbol.
solution_steps: 20% of 50 is 10. Subtract 10 from 50 to get 40.

problems.prompt: A meal costs €24 before a 15% tip. Enter the total without the currency symbol.
solution_steps: Multiply 24 by 1.15 to include the original cost and the 15% tip: 27.60.

problems.prompt: A €80 item has a 30% discount. How many euros are taken off?
solution_steps: Convert 30% to 0.30, then multiply 80 by 0.30 to get 24.

problems.prompt: A €120 purchase has 8% tax. Enter the final total without the currency symbol.
solution_steps: Multiply 120 by 1.08 to include the original price and 8% tax: 129.60.

work.prompt: Show the tax calculation and final total, one expression per line.

problems.prompt: A €200 item is reduced by 15%, then the sale price is taxed by 10%. Enter the final price.
solution_steps: Apply the discount: 200 × 0.85 = 170. Then apply tax: 170 × 1.10 = 187.

work.prompt: Show the discounted price and then the taxed total, one expression per line.
